pages.en:
“True. And I can't compare myself with you either.

“…That is simply the nature of training in magecraft. The only thing we all share is that we place our lives upon the scales.

“The scales differ from one person to another. What matters is how far one is prepared to tip them.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Right. I can’t compare myself to you either.
…Training in magic is like that. The only common thing is that we’re all putting our lives on the line.
There is a difference in how much we put on the line, but it just means how much risk we’re willing to take, right?”

pages.ja:
「その点で言えば、貴方は私なんかよりずっと厳しい。
私、死ぬような鍛錬なんてしたことないもの。そもそも失敗する事がないし」
「
うわ。言い切ったな、いま」

うわ。言い切ったな、いま」
pages.en:
“By that measure, you are far more severe with yourself than I am.

“I've never undertaken training that might kill me. I don't fail in the first place.”

pages.mirrorMoon:
“In that regard, your training is much harsher than mine.
I’ve never trained in a way that might kill me. First of all, I don’t fail.”
“Wow, you just declared it.”

She casually delivers a deeply hurtful pronouncement.

In other words, she said she doesn’t understand how we feel when we fail.

“I never said *this time*.

pages.mirrorMoon:

pages.en:
One day, I would become a man like Kiritsugu.

I continued training for the sake of becoming the Hero of Justice that Kiritsugu said he had failed to be.

Looking back, almost every memory of those days is simply a memory of training in the storehouse.

I have never regretted it.

I must have believed that nothing in the world mattered more to me.
pages.mirrorMoon:
I want to be like Kiritsugu someday.
I kept on training to be the superhero that Kiritsugu couldn’t be.
Come to think of it, most of my memories are about training in the shed.
But I’ve never regretted it.
I’ve always believed that it’s the most important thing for me.

pages.ja:
「……そうか。言われてみれば、そうだな。俺も、それなりにやってきたって事か」

pages.jaRuby:

pages.en:
“…I see. Now that you put it that way, you're right. I suppose I have accomplished something after all.”

“Exactly. You came this far on your own, Emiya. You should have more confidence in yourself.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“…I see. You’re right, now that you mention it. I guess I did my share, huh?”
“Yup. You came to where you are today with your own skill, so have more confidence in yourself.”

Tohsaka makes the declaration with her head held high.

When someone takes that much pleasure in my accomplishments, as though they were her own, I find myself twice as self-conscious.

That and constructing blueprints, along with a few other fundamentals.

There is hardly any point discussing such things now.

The rest is basic stuff like making a blueprint and such.
This isn’t something we have to talk about now.

Accumulation, flow, and transformation of power. That’s my basic power, and I also know the popular spells. I can manage to make a boundary field that’s about a classroom’s size.”

“The Tohsaka family passes down the art of Conversion. Whether the power belongs to me or someone else, transferring it from one place to another is my specialty.

“Magical energy alone cannot produce a Mystery. Before it disappears outside the body, it must be used to activate the formula called magecraft. That makes it difficult to transfer 'pure magical energy' that has not been converted into a spell—”
pages.mirrorMoon:

The technique of conversion is what’s been passed down the Tohsaka family. We’re good at shifting our powers or someone else’s.
Magical energy disappears when we take it out of our body, right?
We cannot create anything special with just magical energy. We execute the equation called magic using the magical energy before it disappears. That’s why ‘pure magical energy’ that’s not part of a spell is hard to move around”

You know that jewels are ‘places’ that easily store thoughts, a prison that stops flow, right?
Additionally, crystals that have been in the ground for a long time carry strong natural spirits. Such jewels can become a simple ‘Magic Crest’ when magical energy is poured into them.
Well, since it’s a jewel, it’ll break once the stored magical energy is released.”

Tohsaka gives a small shrug and returns the jewel to her pocket.
